metadata.title: Gisette: original challenge feature values (Datamonger representation, version 1)
metadata.description:
Lossless portable representation of the original Gisette feature values and splits supplied by the UCI Machine Learning Repository for the NIPS 2003 feature selection challenge. The task distinguishes handwritten digits 4 and 9 using 5,000 prepared features, including distractor probes. The challenge producers had already normalized and centered digit images, constructed pixel-based features, and randomized examples and features. Datamonger adds no scaling, centering, imputation, feature selection, sample exclusion, or label remapping.

The training set has 6,000 rows, the validation set has 1,000 rows, and the original unlabeled test set has 6,500 rows. All features retain their original integer values from 0 through 999. Training and validation retain the original -1/+1 labels and are distributed as gzip-compressed LIBSVM files with a declared dimension of 5,000. Test features are a gzip-compressed CSV with positional columns x1 through x5000 and no invented labels. The original test labels remain withheld by the source.

Nine files are included: train.libsvm.gz, validation.libsvm.gz, test-features.csv.gz, README.md, prepare.py, verify.py, provenance.json, verification.json, and LICENSE. The scripts require the Datamonger repository and its Python development environment. Preparation pins source bytes and checks dimensions, label counts, and source checksums. Verification compares all 67,500,000 feature values and 7,000 labels with an independent source read, and native Rust and independent Python canonical encoders agree. Two preparations produced identical data artifact hashes. These automated conversion checks are not an independent registry-release attestation.

Reuse terms: CC BY 4.0 applies to the data, following UCI's explicit license statement. Credit Isabelle Guyon, Steve Gunn, Asa Ben-Hur, Gideon Dror, and UCI, link CC BY 4.0, and identify this lossless format conversion and compression. MIT applies only to the preparation code and accompanying documentation.

The current Datamonger split decoder exposes the original validation artifact through its fixed test field; task metadata calls it validation. The original unlabeled test CSV is a separate artifact and is not included in that decoder return value.
